key_insight: In children with PANS, pain and fatigue are common and a meaningful subset progress to fibromyalgia-like symptom burden, especially when symptom scores are already high at presentation.
clinical_relevance: Early recognition of pain, fatigue, and cognitive symptoms may help identify PANS patients at higher risk for persistent fibromyalgia criteria over time.
method: Prospective observational cohort of 204 consecutive PANS patients seen at a Stanford clinic
Measured pain/fatigue and related symptoms with the 2016 ACR Fibromyalgia Survey Questionnaire (WPI and SSS)
Used clinician-recorded diagnoses and Cox proportional hazards modeling to assess progression risk
evidence_signal: In this cohort, 42% met ACR fibromyalgia threshold scores at least once and 13.7% progressed to full criteria during follow-up; higher baseline WPI and SSS predicted faster progression.
watch_item: Single-center observational data cannot prove causation, and results may not generalize beyond a specialty PANS clinic population.
paper_title: Prevalence and Predictors of Pain and Fatigue in Pediatric Acute-Onset Neuropsychiatric Syndrome (PANS)
